qt: to the Commission Majbritt Birkholm (PfE) Subject:

Article 4(1) of Council Regulation (EC) No 1099/2009 requires, as a general rule, that animals be stunned before they are killed1. Article 4(4), however, exempts particular methods of slaughter prescribed by religious rites. This is despite the fact that under Article 3(1) animals are to be spared any avoidable pain, distress or suffering. When animals are slaughtered without pre-stunning, they are conscious during the neck cut and may experience pain, fear and suffering until they lose consciousness through loss of blood2. A number of Member States, including Denmark, Sweden and Belgium, have therefore introduced requirements for stunning at slaughter. The Court of Justice of the European Union held in Case C-336/193 that Member States may require stunning which is reversible and does not result in the death of the animal, including during ritual slaughter. In the light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission take the view that the exemption provided for in Article 4(4) remains justified in the light of scientific knowledge about the suffering of animals and the requirements laid down in the regulation to spare animals avoidable pain, distress and suffering?
Will the Commission propose lifting the exemption and the introduction of a blanket EU ban on slaughter without pre-stunning, including where religious rites are concerned? If not, why not?
